---
title: Microstructure-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for High-Frequency Trading
author: Krzysztof Wojdalski
# Annex D dates the title page "Warsaw, July 2020" -- place, month, year. The
# previous format printed a wall-clock build time ("September 2, 2026 02:13
# UTC"), which changed on every render and read as a build artifact on a
# submitted document. Replace `now` with the actual submission month once it
# is fixed.
date: now
date-format: "[Warsaw,] MMMM YYYY"
fig-cap-location: top
format:
  pdf:
    documentclass: pracamgrwne
    latex-engine: xelatex
    mainfont: "TeX Gyre Termes"
    toc: false
    toc-depth: 4
    number-sections: true
    output-file: masters_thesis.pdf
    # Every page number in the contents and the three back-matter lists was
    # low by exactly 4. On the first LaTeX pass there is no .toc, so the
    # contents occupies one page instead of five; the second pass typesets
    # that stale .toc while writing a corrected one, and Quarto's rerun
    # detection did not fire, so the corrected file was never typeset. Three
    # passes converge. Raise this if the contents grows past another page
    # boundary and the numbers drift again.
    latex-min-runs: 3
    # WNE UW requirement 4 indents *every* paragraph by 1 cm, and Annex D
    # shows the paragraph directly after a heading indented like any other
    # (35.6 mm against its 25 mm margin). Pandoc's default suppresses that
    # first indent, which left 136 of them flush at the margin here.
    indent: true
    linestretch: 1.5
    lof: false
    lot: false
    colorlinks: true
    linkcolor: black
    citecolor: black
    urlcolor: black
    toccolor: black
    header-includes:
      - \raggedbottom
      - \setlength{\parindent}{1cm}
      - \setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
      # LaTeX's sectioning commands set \@afterindentfalse, so the paragraph
      # directly after a heading is never indented -- independent of Pandoc's
      # `indent` setting, which only controls whether parskip is loaded.
      # Requirement 4 indents every paragraph, and Annex D shows the first one
      # after a heading indented like the rest. indentfirst restores it.
      - \usepackage{indentfirst}
      - \usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
      - \usepackage{amsthm}
      - \usepackage{rotating}
      - \usepackage{algorithm}
      - \usepackage{algpseudocode}
      - \AtBeginDocument{\let\REQUIRE\Require\let\ENSURE\Ensure\let\STATE\State\let\FOR\For\let\ENDFOR\EndFor\let\FORALL\ForAll\let\ENDFORALL\EndForAll\let\WHILE\While\let\ENDWHILE\EndWhile\let\IF\If\let\ELSIF\ElsIf\let\ELSE\Else\let\ENDIF\EndIf\let\RETURN\Return}
      - \usepackage{mathtools}
      - \usepackage{booktabs}
      - \usepackage{longtable}
      - \usepackage{pdflscape}
      - \usepackage{float}
      - \floatplacement{table}{H}
      # Figures are pinned for the same reason tables are. Each rollout figure
      # is followed by its own Source/Note block, which is ordinary text and
      # does not float; left free to drift, the three rollout figures in Section 6.1
      # moved to later pages while all three notes stayed behind and stacked up
      # under the first one.
      - \floatplacement{figure}{H}
      - \usepackage{tikz}
      - \usetikzlibrary{arrows.meta}
      - \usepackage{caption}
      # format=hang satisfies WNE UW rules 10 and 11, which require a table
      # title or figure caption running past one line to be wrapped
      # "z odsadzeniem uwidaczniajacym slowa" -- indented so "Table 4." /
      # "Figure 3." stay visible. Without it the caption package returns
      # continuation lines flush to the left margin, hiding the label.
      # Annex D sets table titles and figure captions in regular roman at
      # 12 pt: its "Table 1. [Name of the table]Compilation of basic values..."
      # and "Pic. 1. ..." both measure R 12.0pt, and the only bold element of
      # its table is the header row ("a header, which should be written in
      # bold and centered", p. 5). labelfont=bf and font=bf set all 16 table
      # titles and all 5 figure captions fully bold, which the model does not.
      - \captionsetup[figure]{format=hang,position=above,justification=raggedright,singlelinecheck=false,labelsep=period}
      - \captionsetup[table]{format=hang,justification=raggedright,singlelinecheck=false,labelsep=period}
      # ltcaption gives the caption package its longtable support. A
      # longtable's caption is otherwise a row inside the table, so it takes
      # the table's own width and centres with it -- which left seven table
      # titles starting at 36-47 mm instead of the 25 mm left margin
      # requirement 10 asks for. Setting the caption box to \linewidth makes
      # the title start at the margin while the table stays centred, as Annex
      # D shows: its "Table 1." sits at 25.0 mm above a centred table.
      # Both must come after \usepackage{caption}, or \captionsetup is
      # undefined and the render dies.
      - \usepackage{ltcaption}
      - \captionsetup[longtable]{width=\linewidth}
      # \LTcapwidth is what longtable actually consults for its caption width;
      # it defaults to 4in, so on a landscape page the caption box was far
      # narrower than the text block and centred within it. Setting it to
      # \linewidth is what moves the title out to the left margin.
      - \setlength{\LTcapwidth}{\linewidth}
      # Requirement 3 puts every chapter and subchapter title in the table of
      # contents and permits three subchapter levels. The document uses all
      # three (4.5.1.1, 5.3.4.1-4), so tocdepth must be 4 -- chapter plus three
      # -- or those five headings exist in the body but not in the contents.
      - \setcounter{tocdepth}{4}
      # Requirement 14: "line spacing within one entry: single; a blank line
      # with single spacing between entries". Every gap in the bibliography --
      # inside an entry and between entries alike -- measured 7.6 mm, the
      # document's 1.5 spacing, so entries ran together with no separation and
      # each was half again too tall. Pandoc puts the reference list in a
      # CSLReferences environment and spaces entries by \cslentryspacingunit,
      # which defaults to \parskip; \parskip is 0pt here, hence no gap. Single
      # spacing inside, one blank line between.
      # \cslentryspacingunit is only defined when Pandoc emits a reference
      # list, and not before \begin{document}, so the \ifdefined guard is
      # required -- setting it unguarded aborts the render.
      - \usepackage{etoolbox}
      - \AtBeginEnvironment{CSLReferences}{\singlespacing\ifdefined\cslentryspacingunit\setlength{\cslentryspacingunit}{\baselineskip}\fi}
      - \nralbumu{310284}
      - \speciality{Quantitative Finance}
      - \opiekun{dr Pawel Sakowski}
      # Annex D's supervisor block runs over four flush-right lines: the
      # lead-in, the supervisor, "from (name of the supervisor's unit)", then
      # "WNE UW". \jednostka supplies the third; without it the block printed
      # only three lines and the unit was missing.
      - \jednostka{from the Department of Quantitative Finance and Machine Learning}
      # Keywords are lowercased except proper nouns, per the faculty model
      # thesis ("pisane malymi literami - z wyjatkiem nazw wlasnych"; the
      # English edition mistranslates this as "except for generic names",
      # which inverts it -- the Polish governs). TD3 is an algorithm name and
      # stays capitalised. Nine words, against the model's limit of ten.
      - \keywords{deep reinforcement learning, high-frequency trading, order book, single-asset trading, TD3}
      - \newcommand{\keywordspl}{głębokie uczenie ze wzmocnieniem, handel wysokiej częstotliwości, księga zleceń, handel pojedynczym aktywem, TD3}
      # The model prints the Erasmus area as name followed by the five-digit
      # code in parentheses ("Economics (14300)"); 14300 is the same area as
      # the dotted form 14.3.
      - \dziedzina{Economics (14300)}
      - \klasyfikacja{G11, G17, C63}
      - \tytulang{Głębokie uczenie ze wzmocnieniem uwzględniające mikrostrukturę rynku w handlu wysokiej częstotliwości}
  docx:
    embed-resources: true
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
    number-sections: true
    number-depth: 2
    toc-location: right
    format-links: false
    fig-cap-location: top
    css: custom.css
    grid:
      body-width: 960px
    other-links:
      - text: PDF
        href: /masters_thesis/masters_thesis.pdf
        icon: file-pdf
# Annex B, the binding regulation, abbreviates the figure label in both
# languages -- "Rys. 12." in the Polish original, "Fig. 12." in the English
# translation -- while spelling the table label out as "Table 12.". Annex D's
# prose agrees ('starting with the short "Fig."'). Its worked captions say
# "Pic." instead, but that edition is a partial translation of the Polish
# model: its own list of tables reads "Tabel 1.", which is neither English nor
# Polish, and its caption bodies were left untranslated. "Fig." is therefore
# what two of the three English attestations say, including the regulation.
# fig-title sets the caption label, fig-prefix the in-text reference.
crossref:
  fig-title: "Fig."
  fig-prefix: "Fig."

bibliography: ../../bibliography/library.bib
csl: ../../bibliography/apa.csl
# Every source cited by the appendix feature table. That table is raw LaTeX, so
# Pandoc never sees its citations and would otherwise drop from the reference
# list any source cited only there. Keep in step with CITATION_KEYS in
# feature_table_citations.py; `uv run python -c "from feature_table_citations
# import nocite_keys; print(', '.join('@'+k for k in nocite_keys()))"` prints
# the current list. Most are also cited by key in Section 4.2; Foucault2005 and
# Abergel2016 are not, and appear in the bibliography only because of this.
nocite: |
  @Cao2004, @Biais1995, @Cont2014, @Stoikov2018, @Bouchaud2002, @Kyle1985,
  @GlostenMilgrom1985, @Easley2012, @Foucault2005, @LeeReady1991,
  @Boehmer2021, @Engle2000, @Abergel2016, @Wood1985
filters:
  - pseudocode
  - tablenote.lua
  - tableheader.lua
  - tablealign.lua
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: console
  latex_engine: xelatex
jupyter:
  kernelspec:
    display_name: Python 3 (ipykernel)
    language: python
    name: python3

<!-- The faculty model thesis caps this block at 800 characters with spaces and
asks that it not open by stating the aim or topic of the work. It currently runs
770. Keep it under the cap when editing: the abstract page must also hold the
keywords, Erasmus code, thematic classification and Polish title on one page
(requirement 1c). Note that a % comment does not work out here -- this is
Markdown, not LaTeX, and a stray %% block renders as visible text on the page. -->
\begin{abstract}

A Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3) agent controls continuous exposure on tick-level
order-book data from six Nasdaq equities, trained on three sessions and tested
on a held-out fourth. Under frictionless mid-price execution it earns positive
returns with low drawdown and a high profit factor. Independently trained
policies stay active at 0 and 0.01 basis points but collapse to static
positions at higher fees, showing cost sensitivity without a clean break-even;
re-pricing that action path at the bid/ask reverses its sign. Of three feature sets only
the curated ten-feature microstructure state converged, leaving feature choice
unresolved. Only the Differential Sharpe objective produced a trading policy;
the log-return objective did not train, so that comparison turns on whether
optimisation succeeded rather than on what the objective rewards. The
contribution is a reproducible pipeline from order-book features through
Differential Sharpe Ratio reward design to out-of-sample evaluation.

\end{abstract}
